activities.caption: pair each grid part with its job
activities.name: gridAnatomyMatch

config.prompt: The grid's anatomy, plus its canon — pair each with its role:

pairs.right: the gaps between columns, kept identical
an invisible horizontal rhythm every element snaps to

config.why: The better the structure, the less visible it is — a great layout looks inevitable, not gridded.

activities.anchor: headline across eight, caption across four, sidebar three, body seven
activities.caption: call the standard column count
activities.name: gridColumnEst

config.prompt: The standard web grid's column count — chosen because it splits into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths — is?
config.why: Twelve — so a layout can argue 50/50, 33/66 or 25/75 without inventing new numbers.
config.context: The 8-point system applies the same modular logic at hardware resolution: every dimension a multiple of 8 (or 4).

activities.anchor: the luxury-brand manoeuvre: expensive things get room
activities.caption: place the intentional spacing step
activities.name: gridStepPlace

config.prompt: Whitespace discipline: a gap between groups should read as roughly what multiple of the padding inside groups?
config.why: A 1.5–2× step reads as intentional: paddings tight and consistent within groups, gaps clearly larger between them.

activities.anchor: lending rank to whatever it surrounds
activities.caption: bet before the reveal — filling the space
activities.name: gridWhitespacePredict

config.q: A stakeholder points at the page's empty margin: 'there's all this empty space, can't we fill it?' What does filling it cost?
choices: Nothing — empty space is unused inventory
The page's primary grouping signal — whitespace groups, separates and ranks before any word is read
config.why: The squint test tells: a good layout shows a rhythm of dense and empty bands; a bad one shows uniform porridge.

activities.anchor: pattern-breaks are attention technology, spendable exactly once before they become wallpaper
activities.caption: F or Z? file each scanning fact
activities.name: gridScanSort

config.prompt: The eye-tracking shapes — file each fact:

items.label: two horizontal sweeps, then a vertical skim down the left edge
top-left to top-right, diagonal to bottom-left, across to bottom-right
the left edge as the pattern's spine
the diagonal as the main move

config.why: Put the highest-value words where the sweep goes — the first two words of a heading carry the scan.

activities.anchor: tables are honest when cards are decoration
activities.caption: walk the arrangement decision
activities.name: gridArrangementBranch

config.root: A team must lay out a quarterly metrics review for executives. Walk the decision.

start.text: What does the user come here to do?

choices.label: Compare numbers across regions — every cell findable every time
choices.feedback: The answer names the grid: comparison-dense data wants a dashboard — uniform modules, aligned axes.

choices.label: Follow the narrative of what changed and why
choices.feedback: Narrative wants an editorial spread: dominant image, headline with room, pull-quotes as waymarks.

choices.label: Editorial drama in the dashboard
choices.feedback: Pretty, unusable — the professional failure mode is shipping one where the other belongs.

choices.label: Uniform modules, whitespace spent on alignment
choices.feedback: Beauty lives in consistency — the grid serving non-linear scanning.

choices.label: Dashboard uniformity in the magazine
choices.feedback: Consistent, dead — the same failure mode, mirrored.

choices.label: A full-bleed image and stepped column start marking the story's beats
choices.feedback: The flexes mark the argument — asymmetry as authorship.

done1.text: Aligned axes, ordered density: findable every time, for every cell.

done2.text: Sequence and emphasis: the grid serves a linear reading experience.

fail1.text: The row of identical cards answers every content question with the same container — often lazy, sometimes wrong.

fail2.text: Rows of identical cards flatten a narrative into inventory — the card-grid critique in action.

config.why: What does the user come here to do — read, compare, decide, or monitor? The answer names the grid.

activities.anchor: the difference between a broadsheet and a flyer
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the baseline arithmetic
activities.name: gridBaselineCloze

config.text: Set body text at 9.5 pt on %%0%% pt leading: that number becomes the page's universal unit. Captions at 8 pt on the same leading land on the rhythm; a pull-quote at 26/39 occupies exactly %%1%% rhythm-lines; and whitespace is spent in whole units — %%2%%, 26, 39 — rather than eyeballed pixels.
config.hint: One leading, one count, and the smallest whole unit of the spacing.

activities.anchor: which is the question worth a human's time
activities.caption: which curve is the modular scale?
activities.name: gridScaleTrace

config.prompt: A 1.25 (major third) modular scale from a 16 px body — which curve shows the type ladder's growth?

curves.label: A: the same multiplicative step each time
B: the same additive step each time

config.why: 16 → 20 → 25 → 31 → 39 → 49 → 61: each step the same multiplicative journey, so the hierarchy reads as one voice in different volumes rather than six strangers.
